head: 3f4a263548176f1652f9543c0937aa8e5a886422
summary:
The slice's code does what the design and the accepted critique fixes asked. I re-ran the build (0 warnings), Core.Tests (240 passed), Fitness (all 43 rules hold) and window cases T-001 to T-006. T-001, T-002, T-003 (cold open 73.9 ms, 14 rows built), T-004 and T-006 pass.

T-005 does not. It failed 3 of 3 runs with the CPU at 3%: in the rescan phase one UI wait of 680 to 774 ms against a 200 ms p95 limit. The build record says it passed with a longest wait of 47 ms. I traced the cause in a scratch hook copy and a pre-slice exe, both in %TEMP% and since deleted:
- The stall comes from resizing the window while a scan starts. With the window left still, the rescan's longest wait was 10 ms.
- The pre-slice exe (de51999) stalls just as long (419 to 511 ms), so SL-044's code did not cause it.
- The case fails because it takes the p95 over 11 to 20 samples, which makes p95 the same as the maximum.

Separately, the tree's viewport is 39 px at the default window size, about two rows. That is SL-040's 3:1 height split, and the default window height equals the minimum. The builder recorded it as a follow-up; I file it as a finding because it undercuts the slice's purpose.

Coverage gap: no window case checks how a folder that could not be read is shown in the tree. B-007 dropped its check of 12 unreadable rows when the tree replaced the list.

Undeclared drift, all small: the report's topLevel key is now absent on completed endings, rows gain a Note column, and the header text changed. No loop: there has been one build attempt.

Second round: Round 2 found nothing new. Round 1's findings (M1, M2, m1) and its drift list still stand.

This round re-read the changed code looking for ways to break it.
- **Expander clicks keep their state.** T-002 opens rows with SetCurrentValue, but a person clicks the expander. I set the expander's IsChecked in-process, as its click does (the guard refused an automation-peer route, which I then dropped). The row's IsExpanded stayed bound, and after recycling only f02 was open.
- **App boundaries.** The share and bar code survive NaN, above-1 and zero shares. A folder that is empty, unreadable, a link or a placeholder never builds rows or throws. A closed session makes every row blank. StartScan and the ending order leave no path that shows a tree after Stopped, Could not read or Scan failed. A fault in the root's first open ends the app the same way the design's fix does for later opens.
- **Rules and readers.** The new fitness.yaml entries pass both the engine's parser and rules-parity.ps1's settled-entry reader. The `**/*.cs` glob covers files at the Core root. The report's tree reads are guarded when the tree is hidden.
- **Test-side readers.** The fsutil output regex, hook JSON reading, PowerShell hashtable keys and share formatting (culture, AwayFromZero) match what the app writes for every fixture the cases build.

The scratch folders in %TEMP% are deleted and the worktree is unchanged.

findings.claim: T-005, the case behind owed row 6 and O-013, fails reproducibly. The build record says it passed with a longest UI wait of 47 ms. I ran it 3 times on this machine at 3% CPU and got FAILED every time: the rescan phase's p95 was 730, 680 and 774 ms against a 200 ms limit. In one run the first scan phase also failed, at 448 ms. The cause is not SL-044's code. The stall comes from the hook moving and resizing the window while a scan starts: with no moves, the rescan's longest wait was 10 ms. The pre-slice exe (de51999), probed the same way, stalls 419 to 511 ms. The case turns this existing stall into a failure because it takes p95 over 11 to 20 probes per phase: ms[ceil(0.95*n)-1] with n below 20 is the maximum, so one probe over 200 ms fails the phase. As written, the case passes or fails depending on the machine, so it cannot serve as the gate for row 6.
findings.evidence: tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:2507-2513 (Test-T005 asserts p95 < 200 in every phase except open). tests/window/FsaWindowHook/TreeMode.cs:599-608 (Probe.Report: p95 = ms[ceil(0.95*n)-1]). My runs: 'rescan: 18 probes, p95 730.0 ms, max 730.0'; '18 probes, p95 680.2'; '12 probes, p95 774.3'. Scratch-hook toggles: no moves gave a rescan max of 10.3 ms; moves without opening big gave 350 to 678 ms. The de51999 exe with the same move-and-probe loop gave 419 and 511 ms.
findings.fix: Make the p95 mean something: sample every 10 to 25 ms, or lengthen the asserted phases, so each has at least 40 probes, and assert p95 only when probes >= 20. Keep max < 1000 ms as the responsiveness limit. Record the existing stall (roughly 0.4 to 0.5 s on the first resize after a scan starts, present in de51999) as a follow-up for SL-039/SL-040's window, rather than letting T-005 pass or fail with the display state.

findings.claim: The tree the slice exists to show gets about two rows at the default window size. The design put the tree 'in the same grid cell as TopLevelList' without checking how much height that cell gets. SL-040 sized that cell as the minor quarter beside the outcome panel: 3* with MinHeight 292 for the outcome, 1* with MinHeight 84 for the results. The window's default height equals its minimum (620), so at default the tree's viewport is 39 px. In a 1,000 px window it is 134 px (about 6 rows), and about 7 rows maximized on 1080p. Working down from a drive to the folder using the space means scrolling a two-row pane unless the person enlarges the window, and even then the outcome panel keeps three quarters of the height.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml:5 (Height=620, MinHeight=620), :149-174 (row styles 3*/292 and 1*/84). My T-002 run logged viewportHeight 39.135 and T-003 logged 134.135 px at FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT=1000. The build's own follow-up records the same figures.
findings.fix: While FolderTree is visible, give the results row the larger star weight (for example outcome 1*, results 3*, keeping both MinHeights), and raise the default Height (for example 860, clamped to the work area) so the default is no longer the minimum. Re-run B-007 and B-008, which check both lists' full rows at the minimum size.

findings.claim: No case checks how the tree shows a folder that could not be read, although the code branches on it. Before this slice, B-007's Completed ending checked topLevel.unreadable = 12 for New-TopsTree's 12 denied folders. That check was replaced by 'no topLevel in the report' and not moved to the tree, so the no-expander row with the 'could not be opened' note is never checked. T-001's oracle expects an empty note on every row that is not a link. There is also an untested second case: a folder whose listing failed partway gets its children appended and is then flagged Unreadable. The tree shows it with an expander and the note 'could not be opened', which is wrong, because it was opened.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.App/FolderTreeNode.cs:63-66 (Note), src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/Scanner.cs:158-166 (children appended, then AddFlags Unreadable), tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:1858 (B-007 Completed: only asserts topLevel is absent), :2163 (T-001 expects note '' for non-links). The builder's evidence for this branch is a hand run over C:\Program Files\WindowsApps, which no case repeats.
findings.fix: Add a tree-mode read (FSA_HOOK_WALK=1) to B-007's Completed shape and assert that each of the 12 b*-folders draws no expander and the note 'could not be opened'. Word the note differently when ChildCount > 0, for example 'could not be read in full'.

obligations.evidence: MainWindow.xaml.cs:466-467 shows the tree only for a Completed ending; ShowFolderTree is at :356-374. My T-001 run passed: Finished, FolderTree shown, one root row labelled by path, headings shown, TopLevelList hidden. C-002 reads the 150 root children through WALK=1.

The T-001 fixture's size_&_order folder holds sparse.bin (1 MiB in bytes, 64 KiB allocated), dense.bin (128 KiB) and my_file&co.bin. The drawn order 'dense, sparse, my_file' is asserted at WindowCases.ps1:2297; a bytes sort would fail it. Passed on my run.
T-001 checks deep\mid\low, chain\only\end and the root: the root equals the oracle and the sum of its depth-1 rows (WindowCases.ps1:2298-2302). Passed.
FolderTreeNode.cs:43 leaves ChildCount 0 rows unopenable. T-001 asserts the 'empty' folder has no expander. The unreadable variant is not checked by any case (finding m1).

T-001 creates junction j, folder symlink sd and file symlink sf into a folder outside the root. Each is asserted to have no expander, '0 bytes' and 'link, not followed' (WindowCases.ps1:2316-2319). Passed.
T-001's zeros folder holds three 0-byte files. Each draws '0.0 %' with barActualWidth 0 (my run: '0.0 %', 0 px). FolderTreeRowText.BarWidth returns 0 for a share of 0.

The thirds, twothirds, sixteenths (6.25 drawn as 6.3) and tiny (4 KiB under 8 MiB, drawn '0.0 %' with a 1 px bar) rows are asserted from rendered text. FolderTreeRowText.cs:22-23 uses AwayFromZero. Passed.
T-001 checks the rendered NameText of size_&_order, my_file&co.bin and the 149-character name (WindowCases.ps1:2313-2315). The template uses only TextBlocks (MainWindow.xaml:361-377).
T-003 re-run: 100,000 files in big (a child of the root). Cold open 73.9 ms (sort 45.6, build 10.5) in a 134 px viewport with 14 rows built; warm opens 1.3 to 2.5 ms; first row 200 KiB. PASSED.

T-002 re-run: 60 folders, extent 1410 px in a 39 px viewport. f02 opened, scrolled to the end and back twice, parent closed and reopened. Only f02 is expanded, by node state and by container; order and sizes unchanged. PASSED.

T-004 re-run: 3,000-row folder opened 5 times, a depth-3 row selected and focused, second scan started through StartScan. store-released was true while scanning with no tree, and true again after the second ending. PASSED.

T-006 re-run: stop gives report FolderTree.visible=false and the list in view; throw gives exit 70 and 'shutdown tree=False treeItems=0'; a missing root shows no tree. PASSED. The throw half faults mid-scan, before any ending exists, so it cannot catch a tree shown on failure. The real 'Scan failed' ending (MainWindow.xaml.cs:214-236, which never calls ShowOutcome) is guarded only by code reading.

T-005 exercises the designed shape but FAILED in all 3 of my runs at 3% CPU: rescan p95 680 to 774 ms against 200, and one run's scan phase at 448 ms. The stall predates this slice (de51999 shows 419 to 511 ms under the same moves), and the case's p95 over fewer than 20 probes is the maximum. See finding M1.

My read of the obligation aimed at validate-slice: ClearFolderTree (MainWindow.xaml.cs:378-386) closes the FolderTreeSession, and StartScan nulls _result and LastResult (:180-181). T-004 re-run found the first store collectable while the second scan ran, with a row selected. Proven for small stores only; the drive-scale budget re-measure is a recorded follow-up.
Stock TreeView with IsVirtualizing, Recycling and Pixel scroll (MainWindow.xaml:347-351). Expansion is synchronous in OnFolderExpanded via EnsureChildren. No worker thread was built.
PreviewKeyDown='OnFolderTreeKeyDown' (MainWindow.xaml:351) marks Key.Multiply handled (MainWindow.xaml.cs:410-414). T-003 re-run PASSED, including its multiply checks.
FolderTreeSession.cs holds the store and rows hold the session (FolderTreeNode.cs:30). WeakStore and Collected are NoInlining (TreeMode.cs:487-506). T-004 selects a depth-3 row first.
TreeMode.Resolve/Realize (TreeMode.cs:620-644) calls BringIndexIntoViewPublic per level, followed by Settle(Loaded). My T-001 run logged walked unrendered=0.
New-TreeCaseA (WindowCases.ps1:2196-2259) has zeros, thirds, twothirds, sixteenths and tiny. The RECYCLE step is at TreeMode.cs:262-340.
The expand line logs sortMs, buildMs and layoutMs (TreeMode.cs:380-396). docs/design/SL-044-folder-tree.md:124-129 names the lazy IList remedy and says a worker only helps responsiveness.
x:Names on the template parts (MainWindow.xaml:361-377). Rendered() reads the ShareBar ActualWidth (TreeMode.cs:787). CheckTreeRows asserts it within 1 px (WindowCases.ps1:2174-2176).
FolderTreeRowText.cs:22-23 and WindowCases.ps1:2069-2071 both round AwayFromZero. The 1/16 row is asserted.
New-SparseFile measures the allocation with fsutil sparse queryrange (WindowCases.ps1:2086-2107) and feeds it to the oracle. The departure from the listing's AllocationSize is declared.

The IsExpanded setter only records state (FolderTreeNode.cs:102-112). OnFolderExpanded catches exceptions and re-raises them on the dispatcher at Send priority (MainWindow.xaml.cs:392-405). The stand-in row uses FolderTreeSession.None.
.taad/fitness.yaml allow-list rule over src/FsAnalyser.Core/**/*.cs with the corrected except paths. The Fitness check reports every rule holds.
.taad/fitness.yaml has no-view-sort rules over src/FsAnalyser.App/*.xaml and MainWindow.xaml.cs. Fitness holds; the flat list sorts with Array.Sort (MainWindow.xaml.cs:311).
ExpandTimed refuses the root (TreeMode.cs:347-348) and T-003/T-004 use 'big'. The hand-off and rescan-over-tree steps went to T-005 as the decision said, but that case is red (see O-013).

drift: --report schema 1: on a Completed ending, 'topLevel' is now absent because ShowFolderTree clears TopLevelList and _shownTopLevel (MainWindow.xaml.cs:364-366). The design said the report stays unchanged. The builder's declared deviation covers only the added window.FolderTree key. The absence is recorded only in docs/design/SL-044-folder-tree.md:68, and C-002, L-003, M-001 and B-007 now assert it.

The row template adds a Note column, 'link, not followed' or 'could not be opened' (FolderTreeNode.cs:63-66, MainWindow.xaml:374-375). The design's row contract was name, on-disk size, size, bar and one-decimal percentage. Not declared as a deviation.

TopLevelHeader on a Completed ending now reads 'Largest at the top of <root>, by space on disk' or '<root> is empty.' (MainWindow.xaml.cs:367-369). The design does not specify this text and C-002 and L-003 pin it; not declared.

The build record's measurement for T-005 ('longest UI wait 47 ms') does not reproduce on this machine. It fails 3 of 3 runs against an existing resize-during-scan stall of about 0.4 to 0.8 s (finding M1).

cases.evidence: T-001 and CheckTreeEnding: a Finished ending shows FolderTree with one root row labelled by the root path, headings shown, TopLevelList hidden. The case tree has subfolders and files. C-002 walks the root's 150 children. Re-run green.

T-001's size_&_order: sparse.bin (1 MiB bytes, 64 KiB allocated by fsutil) above dense.bin (128 KiB) in bytes but below it on disk. The asserted drawn order is dense, sparse, my_file; a bytes sort would fail.
T-001: deep\mid\low (three levels), chain\only\end (only a folder chain, no files of its own), and the root checked against the oracle and the sum of its depth-1 rows.
T-001's 'empty' folder is asserted to have no expander. The unreadable variant the design lumps in here is not exercised (finding m1).

T-001 creates a junction, a folder symlink and a file symlink pointing at an outside folder holding 1 MiB. Each is asserted to have no expander, '0 bytes' and the note, and no outside bytes appear in any total.
T-001's zeros folder: three 0-byte files, so the parent's rolled on-disk is 0. Each child is asserted '0.0 %' with a laid-out bar width of 0.
T-001: thirds (1/3), twothirds (1/3, 2/3), sixteenths (6.25 and 93.75 midpoints) and tiny (4 KiB of 8 MiB rounding to 0.0 % with a 1 px bar), all asserted from rendered ShareText.
T-001 asserts the rendered NameText for 'size_&_order', 'my_file&co.bin' and a 149-character name, on a 20 px row.

T-003: 100,000 files in 'big', a child of the root, with 50 distinct 4 KiB multiples and the rest empty. Opened cold, then 4 warm, at two window heights. Each open is under 500 ms with at most 200 containers. Re-run: cold 73.9 ms.

T-002: 60 child folders (1410 px of rows in a 39 px viewport). f02 is expanded, the tree is scrolled to the end and back twice, and the parent is collapsed and re-expanded. Node and container expand state are both asserted for every child.

T-004: a 3,000-row folder left open and a depth-3 row selected and focused, then StartScan on a second root. The WeakReference is dead during the second scan and after it. The folder is 3,000 rows, not 100k.

T-006: stop mid-scan gives a report with FolderTree hidden and the final snapshot in the list; throw gives exit 70 with the tree hidden at shutdown; a missing root shows no tree. The throw half faults before any ending exists, so it cannot fail on a tree-on-failure bug. The 'Scan failed' branch is protected only by code structure.
T-005 feeds the shape: 100k files and 20k folders, window moved and resized every 50 ms, the hand-off, big opened, and a rescan over the open tree. It fails on re-run (finding M1).

The design marks it material:false. No window case plants a hardlink; counting once is covered in Core.Tests (ScanStoreRollupTests), and the tree shows ChildRow values without any accounting of its own.
